passage:
Mridul: So your dissertation was due on the twentieth. When did you finish?
Hrithik: The rough draft was done on the tenth. I always set my own date about ten days before the real one. I write it in my calendar in a different colour so it feels real.
Mridul: And then?
Hrithik: On the sixteenth the university's website went down for a whole day, the printer at the library broke, and my supervisor was ill. Everyone else in my class panicked. I was already reading my draft for the third time, changing words, fixing the introduction. I submitted it on the eighteenth. Honestly, the last days were the nicest part.

qa.q: On what date was the rough draft done?
qa.a: The rough draft was done on the tenth.

qa.q: Why did Hrithik feel calm while others panicked?
qa.a: Hrithik felt steady and content, because the draft was already finished and the last days were for improving, not scrambling.

qa.q: What did Hrithik do that gave room for surprises?
qa.a: Hrithik set a personal date about ten days before the real deadline, wrote it in a different colour and finished the rough draft early.

qa.q: How might Mridul be feeling while listening?
qa.a: Mridul seems curious and impressed, and is asking questions to find out how Hrithik managed to finish so calmly.

grounding: A wise worker sets personal milestones ahead of the real date and finishes a rough draft early, leaving room for surprises.

passage: I'm Jaya, and I share the internship desk with Pradeep. Our report was due on the thirtieth, but Pradeep announced a different date: “Rough draft by the twentieth.” It was written on a sticky note above the monitor. On the twentieth, Pradeep printed a messy draft with gaps and read it over lunch. In the last week, when the rest of us panicked because the manager suddenly asked for extra charts, Pradeep just added them, calmly, and spent two days tidying the language. I don't know how Pradeep felt inside; there was no visible stress. I do remember the quiet on the twenty-ninth, when Pradeep was already having tea.

qa.q: What was written on the sticky note above the monitor?
qa.a: The sticky note said, “Rough draft by the twentieth.”

qa.q: How might Pradeep have felt on the twenty-ninth?
qa.a: Pradeep seemed calm and unhurried, having tea while others were busy, though Jaya cannot know the inner state for certain.

qa.q: What did the early draft make possible when the manager asked for extra charts?
qa.a: Pradeep could add the charts calmly and spend two days tidying the language, since the main work was already done.

qa.q: How does Jaya see Pradeep's early date compared with the others' plans?
qa.a: Jaya notices that the others panicked at the extra charts, and probably feels a mix of admiration and a wish to do the same next time.

grounding: A wise worker sets an earlier personal milestone and finishes a rough draft early, leaving room for surprises.

passage:
Week one. Bidisha, twenty-one, had a sociology term paper due on the 30th. This time she wrote two dates of her own on the calendar: rough draft by the 18th, full draft by the 24th. Her friend Santosh laughed. "Fake deadlines?"
Week two. On the 17th she typed a messy, ugly draft, full of notes like "fix this". It felt strange to be done early with something bad.
Week three. On the 22nd, the library's online database went down for two days. Santosh panicked about his paper. Bidisha shrugged; her sources were already in. She spent the last week trimming paragraphs and fixing references, and submitted on the 29th, calm.

qa.q: By what date did Bidisha plan her rough draft?
qa.a: Rough draft by the 18th.

qa.q: How did Bidisha feel when the library database went down?
qa.a: She felt calm and unbothered, since her sources were already in.

qa.q: Why did Bidisha's own dates help her?
qa.a: Finishing a rough draft early left room for surprises like the database outage, so the last week was for improving, not scrambling.

qa.q: How was Santosh affected by the database going down?
qa.a: Santosh panicked, because unlike Bidisha, he still needed the sources for his paper.

grounding: Shows over weeks a student setting personal milestones before the real date and using the final days to improve.

passage: Seema, you're starting your first job, so let me tell you about Pallavi, my classmate from nursing college in Madurai, years ago. I'm your Periamma; I was there. Our case studies were due every month on the last Friday. Pallavi always wrote her own date in the corner of her notebook: the Friday before. "The college's date is for the college," she'd say. "Mine is for me." One month, a flood closed the college hostel for four days right before the deadline. Half of us lost our notes and scrambled. Pallavi had a rough draft done already. She spent those days polishing it at her aunt's house and got the highest mark.

qa.q: What date did Pallavi write in the corner of her notebook?
qa.a: She wrote the Friday before the college's deadline.

qa.q: How might Pallavi have felt when the flood closed the hostel?
qa.a: She was likely calm and secure, knowing her rough draft was already done while others scrambled.

qa.q: Which choice in the story made the difference for Pallavi?
qa.a: Setting her own deadline a week early, so when the flood struck she only had to polish, not start.

qa.q: How did the flood affect the other students in the story?
qa.a: Half of the class lost their notes and had to scramble, stressed, right before the deadline.

grounding: An elder tells of a student who set her own earlier deadline and so had room when a surprise flood hit.

passage: Nirmala, twenty, was working part-time at a bookshop while finishing her diploma in Nagpur. Her final project report was due on the 20th. With shifts eating her evenings, she set her own milestone: rough draft by the 12th. On the 11th, tired after a double shift, she typed until one in the morning and saved an ugly draft. On the 14th her manager, Chetan, asked her to cover an extra three days because a colleague was ill. Once, this would have wrecked her. Now she agreed and still had the draft ready. On her day off, she tidied the charts and the introduction, and submitted on the 19th.

qa.q: By what date did Nirmala plan her rough draft?
qa.a: She set a rough draft by the 12th.

qa.q: How did Nirmala feel when Chetan asked her to cover three extra days?
qa.a: She felt steady rather than panicked, since the rough draft was already saved.

qa.q: Why was the early milestone a wise choice?
qa.a: It left room for surprises like extra shifts, so the final days went on improving the report rather than scrambling to write it.

qa.q: How might Chetan see Nirmala's agreement to cover?
qa.a: Chetan would likely feel grateful and relieved that she could cover the ill colleague's shifts without falling behind.

grounding: Shows a student setting her own milestone ahead of the real date, which leaves room when extra work suddenly appears.

passage:
Sarita wrote three dates on the whiteboard of the college magazine room in Delhi: 10th, all articles in. 18th, rough layout. 22nd, full proof. Underneath, in red: Printer, 28th.
Lokesh laughed. "You've invented deadlines nobody asked for."
"Nobody has to. I asked."
On the 18th the rough layout was done, ugly but complete. On the 23rd the sports writer withdrew his match report, and the cover photo turned out blurred. Lokesh went pale. Sarita pulled in the spare poetry page and reshot the cover in the corridor the next morning. The last four days went on fixing typos and choosing fonts. On the 28th the files reached the printer before lunch.
"Fine," Lokesh said, leaning back. "Your fake deadlines saved us."

qa.q: When did the files have to reach the printer?
qa.a: On the 28th.

qa.q: How did Sarita seem to feel when the report was withdrawn and the cover was blurred?
qa.a: Sarita stayed calm and steady, because the early rough layout left room to swap in the poetry page and reshoot the cover.

qa.q: Which choice worked, and why?
qa.a: Setting her own earlier dates meant the layout was finished before the surprises hit, so the final days were spent improving, not scrambling.

qa.q: How does Lokesh's view change over the story?
qa.a: Lokesh starts amused, thinking the extra dates are pointless, panics when the problems appear, and ends relieved and grateful for them.

grounding: Illustrates a worker who sets personal milestones before the real date, leaving room for surprises and turning the final days into polishing.
